research_questions_addressed.rq1_rationale: Central contribution is a SAPPhIRE/OPAL approach for representing CubeSat conceptual design data across subsystems, including EPS power artifacts.
research_questions_addressed.rq2_rationale: Reports integrability, traceability, usability, and change-management outcomes for system-level CubeSat conceptual design; not EPS-specific reliability/reproducibility.
research_questions_addressed.rq3_rationale: No EPS verification procedure is integrated; authors explicitly state OPAL cannot be an effective requirements verification tool in current state.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Same SpudNik-1 CubeSat/SAPPhIRE behavioral-model lineage as prior work cited by the authors; synthesis should not count it as independent evidence for a separate reference model family.

study_context_population.mission_platform: SpudNik-1 CubeSat; specific CubeSat unit/form factor not reported.
study_context_population.mission_domain: CubeSat low-cost space science context; paper mentions optical payload and multiple bus subsystems but not a detailed mission objective.
study_context_population.organization_type: Academic/student project at University of Prince Edward Island, with author involvement and student design-team data.
study_context_population.project_maturity: Conceptual design end-state at Mission Concept Review; not reported as flight/operational.
study_context_population.eps_relevance_rationale: EPS/power budget is one subsystem model in the multi-subsystem CubeSat OPAL case; no EPS-specific evaluation or V&V.

context_evidence_quotes.quote: All work for this survey took place at the University of Prince Edward Island (UPEI) using the CubeSat 'SpudNik-1' as a case study.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Develop and evaluate OPAL, a SAPPhIRE causal MBSE tool, to capture, manage, represent, share, trace, and navigate CubeSat conceptual design data where behavior-rich data and rapid iteration make conventional PLM/file management difficult.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: High-level CubeSat system and subsystem SAPPhIRE causal models for six SpudNik-1 subsystems. The boundary is conceptual design data/files available by Mission Concept Review. Monetary budgets and schedules were deliberately ignored; file-version evolution was not captured; physical phenomena had no appropriate EPS file.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: The method organizes around system behavior/causality. Participants only received about 15 minutes of SAPPhIRE/OPAL introduction, but causality concepts and SAPPhIRE terms were initially unfamiliar to some users.
other_artifacts: system model scene and subsystem model scenes
generality_reuse_mechanism: specific-mission model with reusable method only

key_evidence_quotes.quote: OPAL is a Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) software tool for the capture, management, representation and sharing of conceptual design data.
All other data, such as monetary budgets and schedules, was ignored for this study.
OPAL-1 Each subsystem representation shall incorporate the original SAPPhIRE Model with all its elements accounted for

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: SAPPhIRE supplies a repeated element structure/template and causal pattern applied across subsystem views, with case-derived method guidance. OPAL also uses a high-level system abstraction and explicit subsystem-interface navigation. However, the implemented model is SpudNik-1-specific and not a demonstrated mission-agnostic architecture, library, open package, or reusable reference model.

evidence.quote: OPAL-1 Each subsystem representation shall incorporate the original SAPPhIRE Model with all its elements accounted for
The system model is a high-level view of the system architecture and allows a user to navigate and view the interfaces between the subsystems.
At the very least, the concept of a simplified representation of an entire system has been shown to be feasible using SAPPhIRE.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture_and_data_flow: OPAL has a system model scene showing subsystem interdependencies and subsystem model scenes based on SAPPhIRE elements. Users select model elements to retrieve spreadsheet sections or launch live CAD/analysis files from a conceptual design files folder.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_continuity: Semantic continuity is provided at conceptual design level by SAPPhIRE causal categories and links between Inputs/States across subsystem models. No robust syntax/exchange standard or lifecycle digital thread is reported.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: Not demonstrated. OPAL supports conceptual design data navigation, not hardware/software integration readiness.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.availability_reproducibility: OPAL, source code, models, link data, and SpudNik-1 files are not reported as available. Implementation details are sufficient for conceptual comparison but not reproduction.

governance_roi_project_decision_linkage.model_derived_performance_indicators_or_: None reported. User-study survey statistics are evaluation metrics, not project management KPIs.

toolchain_fragmentation_interoperability.rationale: OPAL demonstrates central access to multiple file types, but proof-of-concept interoperability remains manual and requirements integration is unresolved.

lightweight_resource_constrained_tailori.rationale: Simplified visual model is evaluated in a low-cost CubeSat/student setting with short training; evidence is limited to one case.

governance_project_deliverables_roi.rationale: Mission Concept Review and conceptual-design cost leverage are mentioned, but no governance/ROI implementation or metrics are provided.

newspace_agile_distributed_rapid_iterati.rationale: The paper invokes New Space and rapid/iterative conceptual design and evaluates change-propagation support.

synthesis_consistency.key_findings_relevant_to_rq1: SAPPhIRE/OPAL represents CubeSat conceptual design data as high-level causal system/subsystem models, linking model elements to design files. EPS appears as one subsystem with requirements, power generation spreadsheets, solar-panel data, power assembly, and power budget artifacts. The method is useful for system-level conceptual data organization but not a reusable open reference model.
synthesis_consistency.key_findings_relevant_to_rq2: Claimed MBSE-related value is mainly traceability, integrated access to diverse files, easier navigation/findability, change-propagation comprehension, and usability after limited training. Evidence is a single SpudNik-1 case and 15-student user study with Likert ratings and qualitative feedback; no EPS-specific reliability, reproducibility, or objective integrability metrics.
synthesis_consistency.key_findings_relevant_to_rq3: No pre-physical EPS verification procedure or MBSE V&V model is presented; authors explicitly state OPAL cannot currently serve as an effective requirements verification tool.
limitations_gaps_stated_by_authors: Physical Phenomena had no appropriate file in the survey and may be more relevant in industry settings.

Requirements representation is very limited; OPAL is not an effective requirements verification tool.
Later lifecycle support and SQL server/concurrent collaboration are future work.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No formal baseline/counterfactual, objective task-time/error measures, or independent validation.
EPS artifacts are included but outcome evidence is not EPS-specific.
Same SpudNik-1/SAPPhIRE lineage as prior author work.
